keywords: Bail application – revision of Magistrate’s order – Code of Criminal Procedure Act Section 404 – Antiquities Act offences – conspiracy – aiding and abetting – destruction/defacing of antiquities – Penal Code Section 113B and Section 102 – interlocutory criminal jurisdiction – bail in exceptional circumstances – deteriorating health condition of accused – medical evidence in bail – prosecutorial discretion – State concession to bail – pending prosecution witnesses – stage of trial – judicial discretion in bail matters – conditions of bail – cash bail and sureties – reporting conditions to police unit – non-interference with witnesses – surrender of passport – custody vs liberty balance – serious offences against cultural heritage – Vander Poorten v Vander Poorten precedent – partial prosecution case completion – fairness of pre-trial detention – Court of Appeal supervisory jurisdiction – revisionary jurisdiction in criminal procedure.
legistation: Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979 – Section 404; Antiquities Ordinance/Act No. 9 of 1940 (as amended) – Section 15B; Sri Lanka Penal Code – Section 102 (abetment), Section 113B (criminal conspiracy-related provision as cited); Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka – Article 138/140 (appellate & writ/revision jurisdiction framework).
